title: controlplane-drift-diagnosis-standup-2026-09-23
content:
Attendees: Priya Nair (owner), Marco Ruiz, Evelyn Chen, Samir Patel, Aisha Thompson, Ben Liao (minute-check-in)

Meeting goal: Quick sync to consolidate findings from the last 48h of anomalous control-plane behavior and surface runbook updates for routing/auth/quotas interactions. Focus is diagnosis + short action list (no long design).

Quick context recap (TL;DR):
- Starting 2026-09-21 ~03:00 UTC we saw an uptick in control-plane API error rates correlated with routing assignment churn and quota refresh storms.
- Customer-visible impact: transient 5xx on token-validate endpoints and delayed route assignment (~200-600ms extra p99); intermittent quota-check throttled requests for some customers on Dedicated pools.
- Hypothesis: subtle drift in allocator backoff logic + a change in auth cache eviction led to synchronized client retries, amplifying load (thundering herd).

Observations / telemetry snippets (raw notes):
- p95 control-plane RPC latency (validate_token) increased from 18ms -> 34ms during peak (09/21 03:10-03:40 UTC).
- Auth-cache hit-rate fell from 96% -> 72% for TTL bucket 60s (prom: auth.cache.hit_rate{ttl=60}).
- Routing assignment publish ops/sec doubled for a 3-min window; manifested as more frequent lease updates (allocator.leases.reassign).
- Quota service returned 429 spikes for a small cohort (10 customers) aligned to Dedicated sudden-burst policy.
- No infra host-level CPU or network saturation observed; CPU stayed at 40-65% across control-plane fleet.

What we tried (experiments & quick rollbacks):
1) Rolled auth cache TTL from 60s -> 90s (canary) on 3 nodes (Evelyn). Result: hit-rate recovered on canary nodes and validate_token latency reduced ~25% locally.
2) Temporary tightening of allocator backoff randomization (Marco) to add jitter to lease reassignments (rolled to one AZ). Result: assignment churn reduced by ~30% in canary; no adverse side effects observed.
3) Throttling bump for quota-service (Samir) to allow more queued checks vs immediate 429s. Result: customer-visible 429s dropped but queue latency increased; acceptable short-term tradeoff.

Unresolved questions (open):
- Was there a recent config rollout that reduced auth-cache TTL for specific customers? (Aisha to check config-rollout logs)
- Do any clients aggressively retry on 429/5xx without jitter? Need to audit SDKs/clients (Priya to assemble list).
- Is there a persistent scheduling pattern that aligns with Dedicated-burst windows? (Marco to correlate Dedicated usage reports)

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Aisha: diff config-rollout logs between 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-22; report any auth-cache related change. Due EOD 2026-09-24.
- Priya: Prod SDK retry policy audit — collect top 5 external SDK repos and flag hard-coded retry loops. Due 2026-09-27.
- Marco: Add randomized jitter to allocator lease reassign path globally gated behind feature flag; produce perf baseline. PR opened: #198; aim to rollout to 50% by 2026-09-28.
- Samir: Implement soft-queue on quota service to reduce 429 blast and add telemetry for queue length; initial patch for review by 2026-09-25.
- Evelyn: Update control-plane runbook (auth-cache TTL recommended defaults + canary checklist) and add a short playbook for re-issuing cache priming. Due 2026-09-26.
- Ben: End-to-end test that simulates 10k concurrent ephemeral token validates with jittered retries; share results. Due 2026-09-29.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Short-term: Keep canary config changes (auth TTL 90s) in prod canary; do not rollback until wider telemetry shows stability for 48h.
- Medium-term: Move allocator lease reassign jitter into default path behind a kill switch; will prefer software mitigation vs capacity increases.

Notes-to-self / informal observations:
- We saw a pattern where quota 429s triggered immediate SDK retry which loops back to validate-token and routing; circular amplification effect. Put a callout in runbook about cross-service amplification and guidance to triage.
- Customer impact map: small Dedicated customers with smaller burst windows got more 429s — likely due to quota shards not evenly balanced. Consider shard rebalance test.
- Keep an eye on region us-west-2 where most canary changes showed better stabilization faster than eu-west-1. AZ scheduling difference maybe a confounder.

Follow-ups & next sync
- Short async updates on the tracker: update PLAT-3421 with each action completion (owners to comment).
- Quick bridge scheduled if any action fails or 5xxs re-appear: 2026-09-24 03:30 UTC (Priya to call).
- Next standup (control-plane ops focus): 2026-09-25 09:00 PT — we'll move to a shorter 20-min deep-dive if any open items remain.

Appendix (links and tickets noted during call):
- PLAT-3421: control-plane auth cache drift (investigation ticket)
- PR #198 allocator lease jitter (Marco) — first draft
- Quota-service soft-queue design sketch (Samir) — gdoc link in PLAT-3421
- Slack thread: #platform-ops / thread ts=1695312000.000400

Rough timeline summary for notes archive:
- 2026-09-21 03:00 UTC: anomaly begins (small scale)
- 2026-09-21 03:10-03:40 UTC: spike window; p95 latency up, 429s appear
- 2026-09-22: canaries applied and partial mitigations; ongoing telemetry monitored
- 2026-09-23 (this meet): consolidated mitigation plan and owners assigned

If anything urgent shows up ping Priya or Marco on Slack. Leaving this as draft until Aisha's config-rollout check completes; will mark final after 2026-09-26 if stable.
